claims.text: The evidence shows that the group for 150.183.249.110 contains a total of 80 matching log lines, whereas the group for 207.243.167.114 has only 23 total matching lines; this means the former generated roughly three‑and‑a‑half times more authentication attempts than the latter despite showing only four sample entries in each excerpt.

Both groups display failures occurring within a narrow time window—multiple failures from 150.183.249.110 are spaced just seconds apart on Jul 10, while those from 207.243.167.114 are spread over about 18 minutes on Jul 26—yet the sheer volume of attempts recorded for 150.183.249.110 makes its activity far more anomalous in absolute terms.
Consequently, the source IP 150.183.249.110 appears to be the more suspicious one because it accounts for a substantially larger share of the total failed SSH attempts across the entire log set.

A plausible root‑cause hypothesis is that 150.183.249.110 is being used by an automated brute‑force script targeting the root account, possibly as part of a coordinated attack against the server’s weak credentials.
